narrative.overview:
Charla is the card a learner hands across a counter, so the screen is a counter with laminated bilingual cards laid on it. The ground is a cool, slightly blue grey; every card is flat white and known by its edge against that ground, never by a shadow or a border. Each card wears a band in the colour of the language it is for: river blue for English, card red for Spanish. The language the learner is practicing becomes the accent for every live state, so the whole app quietly turns blue or red with the direction the learner chose.

One typeface carries everything. Archivo, self-hosted and precached, set semi-condensed and bold for titles and for every line meant to be said aloud, the way a card prints them, and at full width for body, labels and controls. The learner's own language always sits directly under the line it glosses, smaller and in secondary ink. Icons are a single drawn stroke set; emoji appear only as scene pictures in kid mode, where they are content.
keyCharacteristics: Flat white cards on a cool counter ground; no shadows, no card borders.
A language band on every card; the accent follows the language being practiced.
One face, Archivo: semi-condensed bold for what is read aloud, regular for the rest.
Drawn line icons at one stroke weight; emoji only as kid-mode pictures.
Two-language pairs everywhere, the gloss always smaller and under.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: Every card that stands for a language wears that language's colour as a band on its top edge. The band is the only place the language colour fills a region.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Live states use the accent of the language being practiced and nothing else. Green, amber, stop red and teal appear only as the meaning they carry; never as decoration.

rules.name: The Gloss Rule
rules.body: The learner's own language sits directly under the target-language line, in Label size and secondary ink, never beside it and never larger.

rules.name: The Lettering Rule
rules.body: Semi-condensed bold marks what is said aloud or what names a thing. Body prose, buttons and labels stay at full width; no uppercase labels anywhere.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card is known by its edge against the counter. Never add a shadow, a glow or a card border to make one stand out; use the band or the accent tint.

dos: Do give every language-specific card its band, and let the accent follow data-learning on the shell.
Do set anything read aloud in semi-condensed 600 at 18px or more, with its gloss under it at 14px in Ink Soft.
Do keep controls standard: buttons, tabs, inputs, selects, with 44px targets and a visible accent focus ring.
Do keep state colours to their meaning: green for done or confirmed, amber for a notice or a single report, stop red for crisis and destruction, teal for a listed program.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion (all transitions off) and both colour schemes.
donts: Don't add shadows, card borders or gradients; a card is flat on the counter.
Don't use emoji as interface icons; they belong only to kid-mode scene pictures.
Don't set labels in uppercase or add a label above a heading that already names its content.
Don't fetch a font or an image at runtime; Archivo ships in public/fonts and is precached.
Don't let any treatment from kid mode (awnings, stickers, pictures) into the adult app.
